tweet_summary: Elon Musk (240M followers, 139M impressions, 1.3M likes) posts video on Apr 7 2026 captioned 'NASA Artemis passing close to the Moon.' Video shows external Orion-camera lunar-flyby footage with Earth as a distant speck.
why_note_decision: The tweet is TRUE. Artemis II launched April 1, 2026 with a four-astronaut crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) and made its closest lunar approach (4,066 miles) at 7:02 PM ET Monday April 6, 2026 — the night before Elon's tweet. NASA released exterior Orion-camera footage; coverage explicitly identifies Elon's clip as Artemis II flyby video. The original (NMR) note claims this is uncrewed Artemis I 2022 footage — that is a false positive. The community flagged it (noteNotNeeded 747).
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The video is genuinely from the Artemis II mission's lunar flyby on Apr 6 2026. Any note claiming this is Artemis I 2022 footage is a false positive (exactly the original note's failure). FAIL any note that says the video is reused/old/from Artemis I, or that doubts the lunar flyby occurred.

original_unhelpful_note.text: This video is from the uncrewed Artemis I mission's lunar flyby in November 2022, not the current crewed Artemis II mission. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BvWtNx3VOUA https://www.nasa.gov/artemis-ii/
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: incorrect_false_positive: Artemis II launched Apr 1 2026, closest lunar approach Apr 6 2026; multiple outlets explicitly identify Elon's clip as Artemis II exterior Orion-camera flyby footage. The note misidentifies real current footage as a 2022 clip.

fact_check.notes: Artemis II (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) launched Apr 1 2026, closest lunar approach at 7:02 PM ET Mon Apr 6 2026 (4,066 mi), splashdown Apr 10/11. Yahoo article explicitly identifies Musk's tweeted video as exterior Orion-camera footage from Artemis II's closest approach.

importance.lens_rationale: 139M impressions on a major spaceflight milestone (first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17); a wrong CN claiming the footage is fake/old would actively undermine credible space-progress reporting.
